title: A Phase 2 Trial Evaluating the Immunogenicity and Safety of an mRNA-Based Seasonal Influenza Vaccine Candidate Encoding Hemagglutinin and Neuraminidase.
abstract: Influenza vaccines targeting both hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) might offer broader protection than current vaccines, which primarily target HA. This randomized phase 2 study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of an investigational mRNA-based trivalent seasonal influenza vaccine encoding HA and NA from A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and B/Victoria (FLUm3HA-3NA). Participants aged 18–64 years (younger adults) or 65–85 years (older adults) received one of several mRNA vaccine formulations—each containing different influenza A and B HA mRNA doses—or an age-appropriate licensed seasonal influenza vaccine as a comparator. Four formulations per age cohort were tested in part 1 of the study, and one formulation per age cohort in part 2. Day-29 hemagglutination inhibition (HI) and NA inhibition (NI) responses were assessed as primary and secondary endpoints, respectively, safety/reactogenicity as the secondary, and virus neutralization as the tertiary endpoint. A total of 250 younger and 260 older adults were vaccinated in part 1; 161 and 162, respectively, in part 2. All FLUm3HA-3NA formulations induced HI, NI, and neutralizing responses above baseline. In part 1, HI responses against A/H1N1 and A/H3N2 were similar or higher after FLUm3HA-3NA than after comparator vaccination in both age groups. For B/Victoria, HI responses were lower or similar versus comparator vaccination in younger adults and similar or higher in older adults. In part 2, HI responses were similar or higher with FLUm3HA-3NA versus comparators for A/H1N1 and A/H3N2, and lower for B/Victoria in both age groups. In both study parts and both age groups, NI titers were higher for all three strains with FLUm3HA-3NA versus comparators, and neutralizing titers were similar or higher for A/H1N1 and A/H3N2 and similar for B/Victoria. No safety concerns were identified. FLUm3HA-3NA induced HI, NI, and neutralizing responses, with an acceptable safety profile. The results support further development, including optimization of the influenza B HI response. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06431607. Each year, seasonal flu A and flu B viruses infect about 1 billion people worldwide, causing up to 650,000 deaths. Yearly vaccination helps protect against flu. Because flu viruses change over time, vaccines are not always fully effective. New vaccine technologies, including mRNA-based vaccines, are being explored to broaden protection. The available flu vaccines primarily target one key virus protein, called hemagglutinin (HA). Targeting a second virus protein, neuraminidase (NA), could improve protection. We therefore tested an mRNA vaccine candidate designed to target HA and NA from flu A and B viruses. The study evaluated formulations with different flu A and B HA mRNA amounts. The study analyzed 411 adults aged 18–64 years and 422 aged 65–85 years. Participants received either an mRNA vaccine formulation or a licensed flu vaccine as the comparator. The mRNA vaccine induced immune responses to both NA and HA. The NA response was higher with the mRNA vaccine than with the licensed vaccines for the flu A and B viruses. The HA response to the flu A viruses was similar or higher with the mRNA vaccine than with the licensed vaccines. The HA response to the flu B virus was lower or similar with the mRNA vaccine. No safety issues were identified. These results encourage further clinical evaluation of this mRNA HA/NA vaccine, focusing on strengthening the immune response to the flu B virus.

Participants aged 18–64 years (younger adults) or 65–85 years (older adults) received one of several mRNA vaccine formulations—each containing different influenza A and B HA mRNA doses—or an age-appropriate licensed seasonal influenza vaccine as a comparator. Four formulations per age cohort were tested in part 1 of the study, and one formulation per age cohort in part 2. Day-29 hemagglutination inhibition (HI) and NA inhibition (NI) responses were assessed as primary and secondary endpoints, respectively, safety/reactogenicity as the secondary, and virus neutralization as the tertiary endpoint. A total of 250 younger and 260 older adults were vaccinated in part 1; 161 and 162, respectively, in part 2. All FLUm3HA-3NA formulations induced HI, NI, and neutralizing responses above baseline. In part 1, HI responses against A/H1N1 and A/H3N2 were similar or higher after FLUm3HA-3NA than after comparator vaccination in both age groups. For B/Victoria, HI responses were lower or similar versus comparator vaccination in younger adults and similar or higher in older adults. In part 2, HI responses were similar or higher with FLUm3HA-3NA versus comparators for A/H1N1 and A/H3N2, and lower for B/Victoria in both age groups. In both study parts and both age groups, NI titers were higher for all three strains with FLUm3HA-3NA versus comparators, and neutralizing titers were similar or higher for A/H1N1 and A/H3N2 and similar for B/Victoria. No safety concerns were identified. FLUm3HA-3NA induced HI, NI, and neutralizing responses, with an acceptable safety profile. The results support further development, including optimization of the influenza B HI response. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06431607. Each year, seasonal flu A and flu B viruses infect about 1 billion people worldwide, causing up to 650,000 deaths. Yearly vaccination helps protect against flu. Because flu viruses change over time, vaccines are not always fully effective. New vaccine technologies, including mRNA-based vaccines, are being explored to broaden protection. The available flu vaccines primarily target one key virus protein, called hemagglutinin (HA). Targeting a second virus protein, neuraminidase (NA), could improve protection. We therefore tested an mRNA vaccine candidate designed to target HA and NA from flu A and B viruses. The study evaluated formulations with different flu A and B HA mRNA amounts. The study analyzed 411 adults aged 18–64 years and 422 aged 65–85 years. Participants received either an mRNA vaccine formulation or a licensed flu vaccine as the comparator. The mRNA vaccine induced immune responses to both NA and HA. The NA response was higher with the mRNA vaccine than with the licensed vaccines for the flu A and B viruses. The HA response to the flu A viruses was similar or higher with the mRNA vaccine than with the licensed vaccines. The HA response to the flu B virus was lower or similar with the mRNA vaccine. No safety issues were identified. These results encourage further clinical evaluation of this mRNA HA/NA vaccine, focusing on strengthening the immune response to the flu B virus.

The vaccine induced immune responses to both HA and NA, with higher neuraminidase inhibition titers than comparators. title: A Phase 1/2 Trial Evaluating the Safety and Immunogenicity of an mRNA-based Seasonal Influenza Vaccine Candidate Encoding Hemagglutinin and Neuraminidase.
abstract: Hemagglutinin (HA) is the principal immunologic target of most licensed seasonal influenza vaccines. Targeting both HA and neuraminidase (NA) might improve vaccine effectiveness. This randomized phase 1/2 study evaluated an investigational mRNA-based quadrivalent seasonal influenza vaccine, encoding HA and NA of A/H1N1, A/H3N2, B/Victoria, and B/Yamagata (FLUm4HA-4NA). In phase 1, adults aged 18–50 years received either one of twelve mRNA vaccine formulations of varying HA-only or HA and NA mRNA doses, or a licensed quadrivalent seasonal influenza comparator. In phase 2, participants aged 18–64 years (younger adults) and 65–85 years (older adults) received FLUm4HA-4NA (three groups per age category, with different HA/NA mRNA doses) or age-appropriate licensed quadrivalent comparator. Primary endpoints were safety/reactogenicity, and hemagglutination inhibition [HI] and NA inhibition [NI] responses against the four seasonal strains at day 29. Cross-reactive HI/NI responses against drifted strains, virus neutralization, and HA-/NA-specific cell-mediated immunity were evaluated in phase 2 as tertiary objectives. A total of 293 participants (21–25 per group) were vaccinated in phase 1, 480 younger (108–137 per group) and 483 older adults (117–125 per group) in phase 2. Solicited events were more frequent with FLUm4HA-4NA than comparators and were mostly short-lived and mild or moderate. No deaths or vaccine-related serious adverse events were reported. title_zh: 评估基于 mRNA 的 季节性流感 疫苗 候选编码血凝素和神经氨酸酶的安全性和免疫原性的 1/2 期试验。
source_body_en: Hemagglutinin (HA) is the principal immunologic target of most licensed seasonal influenza vaccines. Targeting both HA and neuraminidase (NA) might improve vaccine effectiveness. This randomized phase 1/2 study evaluated an investigational mRNA-based quadrivalent seasonal influenza vaccine, encoding HA and NA of A/H1N1, A/H3N2, B/Victoria, and B/Yamagata (FLUm4HA-4NA). In phase 1, adults aged 18–50 years received either one of twelve mRNA vaccine formulations of varying HA-only or HA and NA mRNA doses, or a licensed quadrivalent seasonal influenza comparator. In phase 2, participants aged 18–64 years (younger adults) and 65–85 years (older adults) received FLUm4HA-4NA (three groups per age category, with different HA/NA mRNA doses) or age-appropriate licensed quadrivalent comparator. Primary endpoints were safety/reactogenicity, and hemagglutination inhibition [HI] and NA inhibition [NI] responses against the four seasonal strains at day 29. Cross-reactive HI/NI responses against drifted strains, virus neutralization, and HA-/NA-specific cell-mediated immunity were evaluated in phase 2 as tertiary objectives. A total of 293 participants (21–25 per group) were vaccinated in phase 1, 480 younger (108–137 per group) and 483 older adults (117–125 per group) in phase 2. Solicited events were more frequent with FLUm4HA-4NA than comparators and were mostly short-lived and mild or moderate. No deaths or vaccine-related serious adverse events were reported. Post-vaccination HI and neutralizing titers in the FLUm4HA-4NA groups were similar or higher for the A strains and lower for the B strains versus comparators. NI responses exceeded those of comparators for all four strains. HI and NI titers against evaluated drifted A strains were similar or higher after FLUm4HA-4NA than after comparator vaccination. HA-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses were generally higher after FLUm4HA-4NA than comparator vaccination. FLUm4HA-4NA showed an acceptable safety profile and humoral and cellular immunogenicity in the study population, supporting further development and formulation optimization to improve influenza B HI responses. Seasonal flu causes serious illness and death each year. Vaccination can help prevent flu, but currently available flu vaccines are not always fully effective. This is because flu viruses change often, so the strains in the vaccine may not closely match the strains spreading each season. Current flu vaccines mainly target one viral protein called hemagglutinin (HA). Adding another viral protein, neuraminidase (NA), may improve vaccine effectiveness. Our study tested a new mRNA-based seasonal flu vaccine designed to target both HA and NA from the four major circulating flu strains. The study had a phase 1 part, analyzing 293 adults aged 18–50 years, and a phase 2 part, analyzing 480 younger adults (18–64 years) and 483 older adults (65–85 years). In each part, participants received one of several mRNA vaccine formulations (with various HA and NA mRNA doses) or an age-appropriate licensed flu vaccine. More people who received the mRNA vaccine had side effects than those who received the licensed vaccines. These side effects were usually short-lived and were mostly mild or moderate. The mRNA flu vaccine induced an immune response to both the HA and NA target proteins. For HA, the immune response was similar or higher than that of the licensed vaccines for two of the flu strains (A strains), and lower for the other two strains (B strains). For NA, responses were higher for all strains. These results support continued development of this mRNA HA/NA vaccine, including improvement of the response to the flu B strains.

title: Non-canonical global dissemination of the influenza A(H3N2) K lineage during the 2025-2026 influenza season.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Seasonal influenza A(H3N2) exhibits rapid global lineage turnover driven by continuous antigenic evolution. However, the emergence of newly dominant H3N2 lineages remains incompletely understood. METHODS: We combined large-scale genomic surveillance with phylogenetic reconstruction, temporal mutation dynamics analyses, geographic dissemination analyses, and structural characterization to investigate emergence and global expansion of the H3N2 K lineage. A total of 170,793 complete human H3N2 hemagglutinin (HA) sequences collected globally between 1992 and 2026 were retrieved from GISAID. RESULTS: We found that the K lineage rapidly replaced previously co-circulating H3N2 J.2 sublineages within a single influenza season. Its global expansion was associated with a non-canonical dissemination pattern centered on the United States rather than the traditional East-Southeast Asia (E-SEA) source system. Temporal mutation dynamics analyses of global surveillance data showed that K-lineage-defining substitutions were first detected in the United States and Japan. Despite accumulation of multiple antigenic-site substitutions, structural analyses suggested preservation of overall HA structural stability, with differential compatibility across pre-existing antibodies rather than complete antibody escape. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings expand current understanding of how globally dominant H3N2 variants emerge and suggest that geographically distributed evolutionary assembly may represent an important pathway in contemporary influenza evolution.
journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases

title_zh: 2025-2026 年流感季节期间流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 K 谱系的非典型全球传播。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Seasonal influenza A(H3N2) exhibits rapid global lineage turnover driven by continuous antigenic evolution. However, the emergence of newly dominant H3N2 lineages remains incompletely understood. METHODS: We combined large-scale genomic surveillance with phylogenetic reconstruction, temporal mutation dynamics analyses, geographic dissemination analyses, and structural characterization to investigate emergence and global expansion of the H3N2 K lineage. A total of 170,793 complete human H3N2 hemagglutinin (HA) sequences collected globally between 1992 and 2026 were retrieved from GISAID. RESULTS: We found that the K lineage rapidly replaced previously co-circulating H3N2 J.2 sublineages within a single influenza season. Its global expansion was associated with a non-canonical dissemination pattern centered on the United States rather than the traditional East-Southeast Asia (E-SEA) source system. Temporal mutation dynamics analyses of global surveillance data showed that K-lineage-defining substitutions were first detected in the United States and Japan. Despite accumulation of multiple antigenic-site substitutions, structural analyses suggested preservation of overall HA structural stability, with differential compatibility across pre-existing antibodies rather than complete antibody escape. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings expand current understanding of how globally dominant H3N2 variants emerge and suggest that geographically distributed evolutionary assembly may represent an important pathway in contemporary influenza evolution.
abstract_zh: 背景:季节性流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 表现出由连续抗原 进化 驱动的快速全球谱系更替。然而,新的主导 H3N2 谱系的出现仍不完全清楚。方法:我们将大规模 基因组监测 与系统发育重建、时间 突变 动力学分析、地理传播分析和结构表征相结合,以研究 H3N2 K 谱系的出现和全球扩张。从 GISAID 检索了 1992 年至 2026 年间全球收集的总共 170,793 个完整的人 H3N2 血凝素 (HA) 序列。结果:我们发现 K 谱系在一个流感季节内迅速取代了之前共同传播的 H3N2 J.2 亚谱系。其全球扩张与以美国为中心的非规范传播模式有关,而不是传统的东亚东南亚(E-SEA)源系统。对全球 监测 数据的时间 突变 动态分析表明,K 谱系定义替换首先在美国和日本被发现。尽管积累了多个抗原位点取代,但结构分析表明总体 HA 结构稳定性得以保留,与预先存在的抗体之间具有差异相容性,而不是完全抗体逃逸。结论:我们的研究结果扩展了目前对全球主导的 H3N2 变异如何出现的理解,并表明地理分布的进化组装可能代表了当代流感 进化 的重要途径。

title: Genomic investigation of an Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K outbreak in a secondary school in Burundi, 2026
abstract: Severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) are an important public health concern, particularly in settings where identification of the causative pathogen can be challenging. Testing of patients with unexplained SARI (SARI surveillance) and characterization of causative pathogens also is seen as an important pillar of emerging disease preparedness. Therefore, we applied targeted viral enrichment sequencing as a tool for understanding a broad range of disease etiologies. In January 2026, an increase in respiratory illness cases was reported in a secondary school in Bujumbura, Burundi, raising concerns about a possible resurgence of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). However, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) testing of symptomatic individuals was negative, suggesting the involvement of another respiratory pathogen. To identify the causative agent, nasopharyngeal samples collected from symptomatic students were investigated using targeted viral enrichment sequencing. Eight SARS-CoV-2-negative samples were sequenced using the Illumina Viral Surveillance Panel v2 on the iSeq 100 platform. Sequencing reads were quality-checked and analysed for viral identification, followed by genome reconstruction, clade assignment, and phylogenetic analysis of the identified viruses. Influenza A virus (IAV) was detected in seven of the eight analyzed samples. Four samples yielded near-complete IAV genomes, allowing detailed genomic characterization. All characterized genomes were identified as Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K, representing the first genomic detection and characterization of this subclade in Burundi. Phylogenetic analysis showed that Burundian sequences clustered into two distinct groups, suggesting the circulation of at least two viral lineages during the outbreak. No neuraminidase inhibitor resistance-associated markers were detected. Influenza sequences were shared through GISAID to support global influenza surveillance. This study shows the usefulness of targeted viral-enrichment sequencing for investigating acute respiratory outbreaks when the cause is not known, particularly when initial testing is negative and routine testing for other respiratory viruses is limited. We provide the first genomic characterization of Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K in Burundi. The identification of different viral lineages highlights the value of genomic approaches to complement routine laboratory testing and support outbreak investigation and respiratory pathogen surveillance in Burundi.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated an outbreak of respiratory illness in a secondary school in Bujumbura, Burundi, in January 2026, where initial concerns about a resurgence of COVID-19 were raised. However, SARS-CoV-2 testing was negative, prompting further investigation into other pathogens. Using targeted viral enrichment sequencing, the study identified Influenza A virus (IAV) as the causative agent, with seven of eight samples testing positive. Four samples provided near-complete genomes, all classified as Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K, marking the first genomic detection of this subclade in Burundi. title_zh: 2026 年布隆迪一所中学流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 K 分支 暴发 的基因组调查
source_body_en: Severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) are an important public health concern, particularly in settings where identification of the causative pathogen can be challenging. Testing of patients with unexplained SARI (SARI surveillance) and characterization of causative pathogens also is seen as an important pillar of emerging disease preparedness. Therefore, we applied targeted viral enrichment sequencing as a tool for understanding a broad range of disease etiologies. In January 2026, an increase in respiratory illness cases was reported in a secondary school in Bujumbura, Burundi, raising concerns about a possible resurgence of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). However, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) testing of symptomatic individuals was negative, suggesting the involvement of another respiratory pathogen. To identify the causative agent, nasopharyngeal samples collected from symptomatic students were investigated using targeted viral enrichment sequencing. Eight SARS-CoV-2-negative samples were sequenced using the Illumina Viral Surveillance Panel v2 on the iSeq 100 platform. Sequencing reads were quality-checked and analysed for viral identification, followed by genome reconstruction, clade assignment, and phylogenetic analysis of the identified viruses. Influenza A virus (IAV) was detected in seven of the eight analyzed samples. Four samples yielded near-complete IAV genomes, allowing detailed genomic characterization. All characterized genomes were identified as Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K, representing the first genomic detection and characterization of this subclade in Burundi. Phylogenetic analysis showed that Burundian sequences clustered into two distinct groups, suggesting the circulation of at least two viral lineages during the outbreak. No neuraminidase inhibitor resistance-associated markers were detected. Influenza sequences were shared through GISAID to support global influenza surveillance. This study shows the usefulness of targeted viral-enrichment sequencing for investigating acute respiratory outbreaks when the cause is not known, particularly when initial testing is negative and routine testing for other respiratory viruses is limited. We provide the first genomic characterization of Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K in Burundi. The identification of different viral lineages highlights the value of genomic approaches to complement routine laboratory testing and support outbreak investigation and respiratory pathogen surveillance in Burundi.

title: Developing and benchmarking one health genomic surveillance tools for influenza A virus in wastewater
abstract: Abstract Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a persistent One Health threat, and whole-genome sequencing from wastewater offers a promising surveillance tool. However, IAV is at low abundance in wastewater, making it difficult to sequence. We benchmark four targeted enrichment methods suited for multi-subtype whole-genome IAV sequencing including custom and off-the-shelf methods. Our custom HA tiled-amplicon panel is sensitive, fast, and cost-effective, making it suitable for monitoring low-abundance seasonal variants of known subtypes, although its reliance on conserved and intact primer-binding sites limits primer design to fewer subtypes. A published universal amplicon method targets all IAV subtypes but performs poorly in wastewater due to its reliance on intact genome segments. Meanwhile, probe-capture methods are resilient to RNA degradation. In real wastewater samples, our custom probe panel recovers whole-genome signals from circulating H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, including validated H5N1 2.3.4.4b reads in samples where dPCR detection is limited. However, probe-capture is generally more costly and labor-intensive than amplicon methods. Across all four sequencing methods, two wastewater matrices, and most spike-in and endogenous virus targets, ultrafiltration-based virus concentration consistently outperforms large-volume direct extraction. Together, these benchmarking comparisons and custom panels provide needed information for implementing IAV genomic sequencing in routine wastewater surveillance.

abstract_zh: 摘要:甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 仍然是一种持续存在的健康威胁,废水中的全 基因组 测序提供了一种有前途的 监测 工具。然而,IAV 在废水中丰度较低,因此难以测序。我们对适合多亚型全 基因组 IAV 测序的四种靶向富集方法进行了基准测试,包括定制方法和现成方法。我们的定制 HA 平铺扩增子面板灵敏、快速且经济高效,使其适合监测已知亚型的低丰度季节性变异,尽管它对保守且完整的引物结合位点的依赖限制了引物设计到较少的亚型。已发布的通用扩增子方法针对所有 IAV 亚型,但由于其依赖于完整的 基因组 片段,因此在废水中表现不佳。同时,探针捕获方法对 RNA 降解具有弹性。在真实废水样品中,我们的定制探针板可从循环的 H1N1、H3N2、H5N1 中恢复全 基因组 信号,包括在 dPCR 检测受限的样品中经过验证的 H5N1 2.3.4.4b 读数。然而,探针捕获通常比扩增子方法成本更高且劳动力密集。在所有四种测序方法、两种废水基质以及大多数掺入和内源性病毒靶标中,基于超滤的病毒浓缩始终优于大容量直接提取。这些基准比较和定制面板共同提供了在常规废水 监测 中实施 IAV 基因组测序所需的信息。

title: Birth Cohort Effects in Adults Associated With Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 Vaccine Effectiveness.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In 2023-2024 influenza season, adults in the 1957-1985 birth cohort had the lowest vaccine effectiveness (VE) against A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses than other age groups, including those in the 1986-2005 birth cohort. We investigated A(H1N1)pdm09 antibody levels in sera collected from influenza cases and controls to explain the birth cohort effect of the low VE. METHODS: Acute and convalescent sera were collected from adults (1986-2005 and 1957-1985 birth cohorts) during 2023-2024. Hemagglutination inhibiting (HI) and binding antibodies were assessed against representative A(H1N1) viruses and hemagglutinin antigens. RESULTS: A(H1N1)pdm09-infected cases in the 1957-1985 birth cohort had significantly lower HI antibodies in the acute sera against circulating A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses than 1986-2005 birth cohort. Over 60% of the cases in the 1957-1985 birth cohort had HI antibodies ≤10 to circulating A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses. Nonetheless, vaccinated cases in the same 1957-1985 birth cohort mounted robust antibody responses to A(H1N1)pdm09 virus infection, suggesting low vaccine immunogenicity. Antibody landscape analysis revealed that these patients born in 1957-1985 with the lowest VE were likely primed with USSR/77-like A(H1N1) viruses. CONCLUSIONS: HI antibody levels in the acute sera were associated with protection against influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 infection. Improving the immunogenicity of the vaccines could help improve VE and overcome the birth cohort effects.

title_zh: 出生 队列研究 对与流感相关的成人的影响 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 疫苗 有效性。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: In 2023-2024 influenza season, adults in the 1957-1985 birth cohort had the lowest vaccine effectiveness (VE) against A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses than other age groups, including those in the 1986-2005 birth cohort. We investigated A(H1N1)pdm09 antibody levels in sera collected from influenza cases and controls to explain the birth cohort effect of the low VE. METHODS: Acute and convalescent sera were collected from adults (1986-2005 and 1957-1985 birth cohorts) during 2023-2024. Hemagglutination inhibiting (HI) and binding antibodies were assessed against representative A(H1N1) viruses and hemagglutinin antigens. RESULTS: A(H1N1)pdm09-infected cases in the 1957-1985 birth cohort had significantly lower HI antibodies in the acute sera against circulating A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses than 1986-2005 birth cohort. Over 60% of the cases in the 1957-1985 birth cohort had HI antibodies ≤10 to circulating A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses. Nonetheless, vaccinated cases in the same 1957-1985 birth cohort mounted robust antibody responses to A(H1N1)pdm09 virus infection, suggesting low vaccine immunogenicity. Antibody landscape analysis revealed that these patients born in 1957-1985 with the lowest VE were likely primed with USSR/77-like A(H1N1) viruses. CONCLUSIONS: HI antibody levels in the acute sera were associated with protection against influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 infection. Improving the immunogenicity of the vaccines could help improve VE and overcome the birth cohort effects.

title: Rapid Identification of H3N2 Influenza A Virus HA-Targeting Antibody Epitopes Driven by Computational Antibody Similarity Measures
abstract: Abstract Antibodies are important therapeutic agents for the prevention and treatment of influenza, and hemagglutinin (HA) serves as the primary target for the development of therapeutic antibodies. However, the identification of epitopes remains an unmet need in the development of such therapeutic antibodies. This study investigates the characteristics of antibody–HA binding interfaces (i.e., epitopes and paratopes) through a computational analysis of all antibody–HA complexes with nonredundant experimentally determined structures from SAbDab, the largest reported antibody structure data set to date. After experimentally identifying and selecting H3N2 HA-specific binding antibodies, a reference antibody library was established. For anti-H3N2 HA antibodies with unknown structures, epitope grouping was conducted based on competitive binding assays that assess interference with the binding of antibodies from the reference library. Based on the complementary relationship between epitope and paratope structures, we selected the structure-based similarity measure most relevant to epitope convergence. Furthermore, we prioritized the experimental validation of binding interference between candidate antibodies and their most structurally similar reference antibodies. We present an integrated computational and experimental framework. This approach includes the construction of an H3N2-specific reference antibody set, computational modeling of antibodies, measurement of antibody similarity, and is complemented by antibody competition binding assays. The dry–wet iterative protocol presented here yielded accurate assessment of the neutralizing potency and breadth of the previously uncharacterized antibody P2A10. Together, the presented pipeline offers a powerful approach for identifying epitopes on anti-H3N2 HA antibodies and for epitope-targeted antibody discovery, while demonstrating the effectiveness of structural analytics in reducing experimental labor.

abstract_zh: 摘要 抗体是预防和预防流感的重要治疗药物,而血凝素(HA)是开发治疗性抗体的主要靶点。然而,在此类治疗性抗体的开发中,表位的鉴定仍然是一个未满足的需求。本研究通过对所有抗体-HA 复合物进行计算分析,研究抗体-HA 结合界面(即表位和互补位)的特征,这些复合物具有来自 SAbDab(迄今为止报道的最大的抗体结构数据集)的非冗余实验确定的结构。经过实验鉴定和选择H3N2 HA特异性结合抗体后,建立了参考抗体库。对于结构未知的抗 H3N2 HA 抗体,基于竞争性结合测定进行表位分组,该测定评估对参考文库中抗体结合的干扰。基于表位和互补位结构之间的互补关系,我们选择了与表位收敛最相关的基于结构的相似性度量。此外,我们优先考虑候选抗体与其结构最相似的参考抗体之间的结合干扰的实验验证。我们提出了一个集成的计算和实验框架。该方法包括构建 H3N2 特异性参考抗体集、抗体计算模型、抗体相似性测量,并辅以抗体竞争结合测定。这里提出的干湿迭代方案对先前未表征的抗体 P2A10 的中和效力和广度进行了准确评估。总之,所提出的流程提供了一种强大的方法,用于识别抗 H3N2 HA 抗体上的表位和发现表位靶向抗体,同时证明结构分析在减少实验劳动力方面的有效性。

title: T cell Cyp27b1 promotes granzyme B expression and antiviral host defense in a mouse model of H1N1 influenza A virus infection
abstract: Introduction Immune cells express vitamin D receptors (VDR) and the CYP27B1 enzyme needed to produce the VDR ligand, 1,25(OH) 2 D; suggesting that perhaps the vitamin D response is regulated locally at the site of infection. Here, we examined the role of immune cell-derived 1,25(OH) 2 D in host resistance to influenza infection. Methods Mice were infected with mouse-adapted H1N1 influenza A virus, to determine the role of CYP27B1 on host resistance to influenza infection. The mouse strains infected include; wild type (WT) littermates, whole-body Cyp27b1 knockout (Cyp27b1 KO) mice, mice lacking renal 1,25(OH) 2 D production (double intronic (DI)KO), mice with T cell-specific deletion of Cyp27b1 (T-Cyp27b1 KO), and mice with T cell-specific deletion of Vdr (T-Vdr KO). Results Whole body Cyp27b1 KO mice developed severe influenza A virus disease, including infection induced mortality, compared to WT littermates. Oral treatments of the Cyp27b1 KO mice with 1,25(OH) 2 D failed to completely protect the Cyp27b1 KO mice from influenza A virus disease. Mice without renal 1,25(OH) 2 D had similar influenza disease as WT littermates. Influenza infection of T cell-specific Cyp27b1 KO resulted in increased respiratory distress and lethargy compared to WT littermates. WT and DIKO mice had more CD8+ T cells expressing higher amounts of granzyme B+ (GrzB) and disruptions in PD-1 than either whole-body Cyp27b1 KO or T-Cyp27b1 KO mice. Discussion The work suggests that renal 1,25(OH) 2 D is not required for host resistance to this influenza A virus infection. The work further demonstrates that immune cells and in particular T cells may produce 1,25(OH) 2 D to locally support CD8+ T cell responses to influenza A virus infection. Defining the mechanisms that regulate local 1,25(OH) 2 D production in T cells or other immune cell types is needed.

Methods Mice were infected with mouse-adapted H1N1 influenza A virus, to determine the role of CYP27B1 on host resistance to influenza infection. The mouse strains infected include; wild type (WT) littermates, whole-body Cyp27b1 knockout (Cyp27b1 KO) mice, mice lacking renal 1,25(OH) 2 D production (double intronic (DI)KO), mice with T cell-specific deletion of Cyp27b1 (T-Cyp27b1 KO), and mice with T cell-specific deletion of Vdr (T-Vdr KO). Results Whole body Cyp27b1 KO mice developed severe influenza A virus disease, including infection induced mortality, compared to WT littermates. Oral treatments of the Cyp27b1 KO mice with 1,25(OH) 2 D failed to completely protect the Cyp27b1 KO mice from influenza A virus disease. Mice without renal 1,25(OH) 2 D had similar influenza disease as WT littermates. Influenza infection of T cell-specific Cyp27b1 KO resulted in increased respiratory distress and lethargy compared to WT littermates. WT and DIKO mice had more CD8+ T cells expressing higher amounts of granzyme B+ (GrzB) and disruptions in PD-1 than either whole-body Cyp27b1 KO or T-Cyp27b1 KO mice. Discussion The work suggests that renal 1,25(OH) 2 D is not required for host resistance to this influenza A virus infection. The work further demonstrates that immune cells and in particular T cells may produce 1,25(OH) 2 D to locally support CD8+ T cell responses to influenza A virus infection. Defining the mechanisms that regulate local 1,25(OH) 2 D production in T cells or other immune cell types is needed.

title: Risk of Hospitalization Related to Influenza A(H3N2) Virus Subclade K, Thailand, June-December 2025.
abstract: Antigenically drifted influenza A(H3N2) subclade K viruses have contributed substantially to influenza burden since 2025, but their clinical severity is less well described. Using sentinel surveillance data from Thailand, we found no significant difference in the adjusted odds of hospitalization among those infected with subclade K versus other influenza viruses (adjusted odds ratio 1.06, 95% CI .67, 1.68). This approach to estimating hospitalization risk for an emerging influenza virus subclade using sentinel surveillance data could serve as a model for conducting future rapid assessments. Summary Using sentinel respiratory surveillance data from Thailand, this paper found no large, significant difference in hospitalization risk for patients infected with influenza A(H3N2) subclade K compared with other influenza viruses.

title: Sex and age differences in antibody responses to seasonal influenza vaccination are mediated by estrogenic upregulation of NF-κB and TNF signaling in B cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Sex differences in the humoral immune responses to the seasonal quadrivalent influenza vaccine (QIV) in young adults (YA; 18–49 years old) or high-dose QIV in old adults (OA; 75+ years old) were analyzed to determine how age-related changes, including in steroids, impact sex differences in B cells. Among YAs, females had greater H3N2, but not H1N1, neutralizing antibody titers, and greater proportions of hemagglutinin (HA)+ CD19+ B cells and HA+ memory B cells than males through 28 days post-vaccination (DPV), that was not observed among OAs. Machine learning algorithms illustrated that baseline (0 DPV) steroids, including 17-hydroxyprogesterone, estrogens, and testosterone, as well as HA+ CD19+ B cells and HA+ antibody-secreting B cells (ASCs), were major predictors of seroconversion at 28 DPV, particularly in YA. Single-cell RNA sequencing demonstrated that CD19+ B cells from YA females had greater transcriptional activity at 7 DPV than YA males, with upregulation of genes with estrogen-response elements (EREs) along NF-κB-mediated TNF signaling pathways in B-cell subsets, which was mitigated in OA. Estradiol treatment of ASCs from YA females, but not males, increased the number and size of HA+ IgG+ cells and expression of ERE genes along the NF-κB-mediated TNF signaling pathway,that was inhibited by an estrogen receptor antagonist. Pharmacological inhibition of either NF-κB or TNF signaling blocked the ability of E2 to upregulate antibody secretion in cells from YA females. This study provides mechanistic insights into estrogen-mediated increases in influenza vaccine-induced antibody responses among reproductive-aged females and suggests a role for estrogen signaling in the reduction of sex differences in vaccine-induced immunity with old age. IMPORTANCE Sex differences in influenza vaccine-induced immune responses become less pronounced with old age, which we hypothesize could be related to changes in circulating gonadal steroids. analysis.summary_en: This study explores how sex differences in antibody responses to seasonal influenza vaccination are influenced by estrogenic upregulation of NF-κB and TNF signaling in B cells. It analyzed responses in young adults (YA; 18–49 years) and old adults (OA; 75+ years) after receiving the quadrivalent influenza vaccine (QIV). The research found that YA females had greater neutralizing antibody titers and more HA+ B cells compared to males, with these differences mitigated in OAs. abstract_zh: 摘要:分析了年轻人(YA;18-49 岁)中体液 免疫应答 与季节性四价流感 疫苗 (QIV) 或老年人(OA;75 岁以上)中高剂量 QIV 的性别差异,以确定年龄相关的变化(包括类固醇的变化)如何影响 B 细胞的性别差异。在 YAs 中,疫苗接种 (DPV) 后 28 天,女性的 H3N2 水平、中和抗体滴度、血凝素 (HA)+ CD19+ B 细胞和 HA+ 记忆 B 细胞的比例高于男性,但没有 H1N1,而在 OA 中未观察到这一点。机器学习算法表明,基线 (0 DPV) 类固醇,包括 17-羟基孕酮、雌激素和睾酮,以及 HA+ CD19+ B 细胞和 HA+ 抗体分泌 B 细胞 (ASC),是 28 DPV 时血清转化的主要预测因子,尤其是在 YA 中。单细胞 RNA 测序表明,YA 女性的 CD19+ B 细胞在 7 DPV 时比 YA 男性具有更高的转录活性,B 细胞亚群中雌激素反应元件 (ERE) 沿着 NF-κB 介导的 TNF 信号通路的基因上调,而在 OA 中这种情况有所减轻。来自 YA 女性(而非男性)的 ASC 中的雌二醇 治疗 增加了 HA+ IgG+ 细胞的数量和大小,以及 NF-κB 介导的 TNF 信号通路中 ERE 基因的表达,而雌激素受体拮抗剂可抑制这种情况。NF-κB 或 TNF 信号传导的药理抑制可阻断 E2 上调 YA 雌性细胞中抗体分泌的能力。这项研究提供了育龄女性中雌激素介导的流感 疫苗 诱导的抗体反应增加的机制见解,并表明雌激素信号在减少 疫苗 诱导的老年免疫性别差异中的作用。重要性随着年龄的增长,流感 疫苗 诱导的 免疫应答 的性别差异变得不那么明显,我们假设这可能与循环性腺类固醇的变化有关。我们的研究表明,在接受 季节性流感 疫苗 后,雌激素活性升高的年轻成年女性有更多识别流感血凝素的 B 细胞;他们的 B 细胞在雌激素信号传导和炎症通路上具有更强的活性,并且比年轻成年男性产生更强的抗体反应,而这些性别差异在老年人中得到了缓解。我们通过证明离体雌二醇通过雌激素受体和与 NF-κB 的结合增加 B 细胞的抗体产生,确定雌激素是流感免疫性别差异的关键驱动因素。这些发现有助于解释 疫苗 免疫力性别差异的生物学基础,并表明荷尔蒙环境,而不仅仅是实际年龄,决定了一个人对 疫苗 的反应。

title: Differentiating Avian and Seasonal Influenza Viruses in Wastewater by Digital PCR
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5Nx) viruses, particularly clade 2.3.4.4b, pose substantial global health risks. We combined and piloted 2 duplex reverse transcription digital PCRs to discriminate between avian and seasonal influenza viruses in wastewater. This approach enabled rapid, strain-specific detection to reduce ambiguity in environmental surveillance for influenza viruses.

title: Bat-borne influenza A H9N2 virus shows species-specific replication and transmission
abstract: Bat-borne H9N2 IAV (bat H9N2), initially detected in bat feces in Egypt in 2017, has recently attracted attention because of its unexpected pre-pandemic properties, including airborne transmission between ferrets and efficient replication in human lung explant cultures. However, its host range and potential reservoir hosts remain poorly defined, particularly with respect to additional bat hosts and mammalian or avian mixing-vessel species. Here, we compare the susceptibility of two pteropodid bat species, Rousettus aegyptiacus and Eidolon helvum, and additionally assessed pigs and quails following intranasal inoculation with bat H9N2. aegyptiacus showed only low-level viral replication and shedding, largely restricted to the upper respiratory tract, and did not show transmission to contact bats. In contrast, both juvenile and adult E. helvum, despite showing no clinical signs, showed high-level viral replication and shedding in the upper respiratory tract, with efficient and early transmission to contact bats. Viral RNA was most abundant in the respiratory turbinates, the nasopharyngeal meatus and the tracheal epithelium, where it was associated with moderate to severe necrotizing rhinitis and tracheitis. The lower respiratory tract was less involved, with viral RNA confined to scattered bronchioles and associated with focal necrotizing bronchiolitis. Other organs, including the gastrointestinal tract, lacked histologic lesions and viral RNA labeling. In pigs and quails, intranasal inoculation did not result in detectable replication, transmission, or seroconversion. Our findings demonstrate marked differences in the susceptibility to bat H9N2 between the two fruit bat species tested and identify E. helvum as a highly susceptible host capable of rapid and efficient transmission. Conversely, pigs and quails were not susceptible, suggesting that additional viral adaptations may be required to allow for a productive infection in these species.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the host range and transmission potential of bat-borne H9N2 influenza A virus (IAV), as it has shown unexpected pre-pandemic properties, including airborne transmission between ferrets and efficient replication in human lung explant cultures.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compared the susceptibility of two pteropodid bat species, Rousettus aegyptiacus and Eidolon helvum, and also assessed pigs and quails following intranasal inoculation with bat H9N2.
analysis.methods: The researchers intranasally inoculated the animals and assessed viral replication, shedding, and transmission through examination of viral RNA levels in various tissues and observation of clinical signs.
analysis.main_results: Rousettus aegyptiacus showed only low-level viral replication and shedding, largely restricted to the upper respiratory tract, and did not show transmission to contact bats. In contrast, both juvenile and adult Eidolon helvum showed high-level viral replication and shedding in the upper respiratory tract, with efficient and early transmission to contact bats.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate marked differences in susceptibility to bat H9N2 between the two fruit bat species tested and identify Eidolon helvum as a highly susceptible host capable of rapid and efficient transmission.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the importance of understanding the host range of bat-borne H9N2 IAV for surveillance and risk assessment, particularly in identifying potential reservoir hosts and mixing-vessel species.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the host range and transmission potential of bat-borne H9N2 influenza A virus (IAV), which has shown unexpected pre-pandemic properties. The researchers compared the susceptibility of two fruit bat species, Rousettus aegyptiacus and Eidolon helvum, as well as pigs and quails, following intranasal inoculation. Results showed that R. aegyptiacus had low-level viral replication and no transmission, while E. helvum exhibited high-level replication and efficient transmission. These findings suggest that E. helvum may be a significant host for bat H9N2 IAV, with implications for surveillance and risk assessment. The study's limitations include a small sample size and focus on specific animal models, but the evidence is strong based on direct observations of viral behavior.

abstract_zh: 蝙蝠传播的 H9N2 IAV (bat H9N2) 最初于 2017 年在埃及的蝙蝠粪便中检测到,最近因其意想不到的大流行前特性而引起关注,包括雪貂之间的空气传播 传播 以及在人类肺外植体培养物中的有效复制。然而,其 宿主 范围和潜在的 宿主 宿主 的定义仍然不明确,特别是对于其他蝙蝠 宿主 和哺乳动物或鸟类混合容器物种。在这里,我们比较了两种翼足类蝙蝠物种 Rousettus aegyptiacus 和 Eidolon helvum 的敏感性,并另外评估了鼻内接种蝙蝠 H9N2 后的猪和鹌鹑。埃及伊蚊仅表现出低水平的病毒复制和脱落,很大程度上局限于上呼吸道,并且没有表现出传播接触蝙蝠。相比之下,幼年和成年的鼠疫,尽管没有表现出任何临床症状,但在上呼吸道中表现出高水平的病毒复制和脱落,并能有效且早期地接触蝙蝠。病毒RNA在呼吸道鼻甲、鼻咽道和气管上皮中最为丰富,与中度至重度坏死性鼻炎和气管炎有关。下呼吸道受累较少,病毒RNA局限于分散的细支气管,并与局灶性坏死性细支气管炎相关。其他器官,包括胃肠道,缺乏组织学病变和病毒 RNA 标记。在猪和鹌鹑中,鼻内接种不会导致可检测到的复制、传播 或血清转化。我们的研究结果表明,所测试的两种果蝠物种之间对蝙蝠 H9N2 的易感性存在显着差异,并将 E. helvum 鉴定为高度易感的 宿主,能够快速有效地进行 传播。相反,猪和鹌鹑不受影响,这表明可能需要额外的病毒适应才能在这些物种中产生有效的感染。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,所测试的两种果蝠物种之间对蝙蝠 H9N2 的易感性存在显着差异,并将 Eidolon helvum 确定为高度易感的 宿主,能够快速有效地进行 传播。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了了解蝙蝠传播的 H9N2 IAV 的 宿主 范围对于 监测 和风险评估的重要性,特别是在识别潜在的 储存宿主 宿主 和混合容器物种方面。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于少量动物的体内实验,不包括长期监测或更广泛的 宿主 物种,但由于对复制、脱落和 传播 的直接观察,证据有力。

title: Fitness flux in SARS-CoV-2 and influenza H3N2
abstract: The tempo of viral adaptation is usually read indirectly from the composition of mutations, through measures such as dN/dS. Here we measure it directly from the dynamics of variant frequencies, where we use multinomial logistic regression to estimate a fitness for each co-circulating variant. We aggregate these estimates to derive the rate of change of mean population fitness, referred to as fitness flux. Tracing SARS-CoV-2 from its emergence, we find that it initially adapted rapidly, doubling in fitness every 6 months from Jan 2021 to Jun 2022, but slowing to every 2.4 years from Jul 2022 to Dec 2025. Seasonal influenza H3N2 sustained a slower, steadier pace doubling in fitness every 10.0 years. In both, the rate of fitness gain closely tracks the variance in fitness, matching the 1:1 expectation of Fisher’s fundamental theorem. Phylogenetic contrasts between parent and child lineages localize most fitness gain to spike, and within spike to the receptor-binding domain, where a simple count of spike S1 substitutions predicts lineage fitness about as well as deep-learning escape and protein-language-model scores. Measuring fitness directly thus offers a transparent, frequency-based alternative to mutational proxies for tracking and anticipating viral adaptation. The website blab.github.io/fitness-flux/ is the intended reading experience of this paper, providing responsive layout and interactive figures.

abstract_original: The tempo of viral adaptation is usually read indirectly from the composition of mutations, through measures such as dN/dS. Here we measure it directly from the dynamics of variant frequencies, where we use multinomial logistic regression to estimate a fitness for each co-circulating variant. We aggregate these estimates to derive the rate of change of mean population fitness, referred to as fitness flux. Tracing SARS-CoV-2 from its emergence, we find that it initially adapted rapidly, doubling in fitness every 6 months from Jan 2021 to Jun 2022, but slowing to every 2.4 years from Jul 2022 to Dec 2025. Seasonal influenza H3N2 sustained a slower, steadier pace doubling in fitness every 10.0 years. In both, the rate of fitness gain closely tracks the variance in fitness, matching the 1:1 expectation of Fisher’s fundamental theorem. Phylogenetic contrasts between parent and child lineages localize most fitness gain to spike, and within spike to the receptor-binding domain, where a simple count of spike S1 substitutions predicts lineage fitness about as well as deep-learning escape and protein-language-model scores. Measuring fitness directly thus offers a transparent, frequency-based alternative to mutational proxies for tracking and anticipating viral adaptation. The website blab.github.io/fitness-flux/ is the intended reading experience of this paper, providing responsive layout and interactive figures.

title: A review of fractional calculus models for avian influenza: Dynamics, memory effects, and control perspectives
abstract: Avian influenza is a serious global public health threat, and both humans and animals can be infected. Classical integer-order compartmental models are generally not capable of capturing the complex temporal dynamics of epidemic systems, especially memory-dependent phenomena such as delayed immune response and environmental virus persistence. In this review, we have surveyed the use of fractional calculus in the modeling of avian influenza epidemics with emphasis on disease transmission, memory effects, and intervention strategies. In detail, we consider four fractional operators, namely, the Caputo, Caputo-Fabrizio, Atangana-Baleanu, and fractal-fractional operators, and compare the structures of their kernels and their memory properties. We review progress in data-driven modeling, including calibration to real epidemic surveillance data, seasonal transmission patterns, and fractional optimal control formulations in a One Health framework. Based on the review of 16 studies combining fractional calculus with avian influenza or influenza transmission modeling, consistent evidence is provided that fractional-order models reproduce the real outbreak dynamics better than the classical ones. As far as surveillance data is concerned, the Atangana-Baleanu-Caputo operator yields the fewest prediction errors. Key research gaps are identified, and future directions are proposed, including hybrid fractional-machine learning frameworks for real-time adaptive forecasting.
journal: An International Journal of Optimization and Control Theories & Applications (IJOCTA)

title: Lineage Dynamics and Risk Factors Underlying Serotype 4 Invasive Pneumococcal Disease in Spain.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The emergence of vaccine-covered serotypes causing invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) is a serious concern worldwide. METHODS: We characterized all national serotype 4 IPD isolates from children and adults received at the Spanish Pneumococcal Reference Laboratory (2009-2024). RESULTS: We investigated the unexpected rise of serotype 4 causing IPD in young adults after the COVID-19 pandemic, affecting the elderly population in recent years. Epidemiological and genomic analysis confirmed that the rise started as an abrupt cluster of cases in Seville (Andalusia) in the year 2022 due to the ST15063 within the GPSC12 lineage. This outbreak initially affected nonvaccinated young individuals associated with high rates of tobacco smoking, alcohol, and inhaled drugs followed by a general distribution through the country in the following years that affected adults ≥65 years old. Moreover, ST15063 serotype 4 strains displayed enhanced infection rates of human lung cells that significantly increased in the presence of cigarette smoke exposure and by influenza A(H3N2) coinfection. CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the need for targeted vaccination strategies, molecular surveillance, and focused interventions in high-risk populations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the rise of serotype 4 invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) in Spain, particularly in young adults after the COVID-19 pandemic. The research focuses on the epidemiological and genomic characteristics of the ST15063 lineage within the GPSC12 group, which was identified as the cause of an abrupt cluster of cases in Seville in 2022. The outbreak initially affected nonvaccinated young individuals with high rates of tobacco smoking, alcohol, and inhaled drug use, followed by a broader distribution affecting adults aged ≥65 years. The study also found that these strains showed increased infection rates in human lung cells, especially under cigarette smoke exposure and influenza A(H3N2) coinfection. The authors emphasize the importance of targeted vaccination strategies, molecular surveillance, and interventions in high-risk populations. The evidence is based on isolates from the Spanish Pneumococcal Reference Laboratory between 2009 and 2024, and the findings are interpreted as highlighting the need for focused public health measures. The study's limitations include its focus on serotype 4 IPD and the absence of detailed statistical or laboratory procedures.

title: Disruption of the polyuracil tract can greatly enhance immunostimulatory properties of influenza delVGs
abstract: Non-standard viral genomes (nsVGs) are replication-incompetent genomes within viral populations whose presence has been associated with an enhanced immune response. This association has garnered interest in their use as potential antivirals, vaccine adjuvants, or general immune-modulators. In influenza A virus (IAV), the predominant nsVG is a large deletion in one of the three polymerase segments, which results in deletion-containing viral genomes (delVGs). Work from our group has found that individual delVGs can be recovered that are capable of stimulating high levels of interferon, however we and others have not previously found any consistent means of predicting or modifying determinants of this stimulation. Using high-throughput genetic approaches, we find that specific mutations disrupting the polyuracil tract in IAV delVGs can enhance interferon production by up to two orders of magnitude. Such variants can also associate with improved rescue in artificial systems engineered to exclude infectious virus, and can greatly suppress the growth of replication-competent virus. These findings indicate the polyuracil tract is a key, and unexpected, target for improvement of immunostimulatory delVGs derived from IAV.

title_zh: 多尿嘧啶束的破坏可以大大增强流感 delVG 的免疫刺激特性
source_body_en: Non-standard viral genomes (nsVGs) are replication-incompetent genomes within viral populations whose presence has been associated with an enhanced immune response. This association has garnered interest in their use as potential antivirals, vaccine adjuvants, or general immune-modulators. In influenza A virus (IAV), the predominant nsVG is a large deletion in one of the three polymerase segments, which results in deletion-containing viral genomes (delVGs). Work from our group has found that individual delVGs can be recovered that are capable of stimulating high levels of interferon, however we and others have not previously found any consistent means of predicting or modifying determinants of this stimulation. Using high-throughput genetic approaches, we find that specific mutations disrupting the polyuracil tract in IAV delVGs can enhance interferon production by up to two orders of magnitude. Such variants can also associate with improved rescue in artificial systems engineered to exclude infectious virus, and can greatly suppress the growth of replication-competent virus. These findings indicate the polyuracil tract is a key, and unexpected, target for improvement of immunostimulatory delVGs derived from IAV.

title: Evolutionary reconstruction of bat influenza A viruses reveals segment-specific histories and host-associated selection
abstract: Abstract Influenza A (IAV) is a major zoonotic pathogen infecting a broad range of vertebrate hosts. In this study, we focus on inferring the evolutionary history of a subset of novel IAV, isolated from New World bats, which use a non-canonical host receptor and infer their relationship to sialic-acid-binding IAV. Little is known about when these novel subtypes emerged and how selection has acted upon them compared to sialic-acid-binding circulating strains. The current state of the field is split on whether bats are natural reservoirs for a distinct yet low abundance IAV lineage, or if influenza underwent rapid evolution after a recent spillover from a species within its standard host range. By analyzing segment-specific phylogenies, we hope to clarify the evolutionary history of bat IAV. Our objectives are to infer the date of divergence of non-canonical bat IAV from sialic-acid binding IAV, identify patterns of selection acting on bat IAV compared to representative samples of sialic-acid-binding IAV to identify potential signatures of genome-wide adaptation, and finally to reconstruct ancestral state transitions to infer which host taxa preceded spillover into bats. To accomplish this, we analyzed each IAV genome segment independently using least-squares molecular dating, Bayesian discrete-trait ancestral host reconstruction, and branch-site selection tests. Our results suggest that non-canonical bat IAV diverged from major IAV lineages 100-200 years ago, supporting a deeper evolutionary history rather than a very recent spillover event. However, discordance among genome segments in inferred divergence times, selective pressures, and ancestral hosts indicates that bat IAV experienced segment-specific evolutionary histories. Together, these findings suggest that non-canonical bat IAV represents a deeply divergent lineage with a complex evolutionary history involving segment-specific selection and host-transition dynamics.

title: Mixed Pneumonia with Pulmonary Embolism and Multiple Pathogens Detected in Bronchoalveolar Lavage Fluid: A Case Report.
abstract: Severe community-acquired pneumonia may involve mixed pathogens and concurrent vascular complications. A 72-year-old man presented with fever, nonproductive cough, vomiting, hypoxemia, markedly elevated inflammatory markers, and an elevated D-dimer concentration. Chest computed tomography showed left lower-lobe consolidation and pleural effusion. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography, obtained because of hypoxemia and suspected pulmonary embolism, showed a filling defect in a right upper-lobe pulmonary artery. The patient received antimicrobial therapy prior to bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL). Bronchoscopy was performed in the bronchopulmonary segment corresponding to the radiographic lesion, and approximately 10 mL of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) was recovered aseptically for microbiological and cytological testing. An aliquot of at least 3 mL was allocated to a multiplex pathogen-targeted sequencing assay, which detected Chlamydia psittaci, influenza A H3N2, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and additional conditionally pathogenic or commensal organisms. The three principal detections were interpreted in conjunction with the clinical presentation, imaging, inflammatory markers, BALF cytology, conventional testing, and treatment response. The patient improved during antimicrobial and anticoagulant treatment and was discharged on December 3, 2025. At the documented outpatient follow-up on December 17, rivaroxaban was continued for approximately one further month. This case highlights the adjunctive value and interpretive limitations of targeted sequencing in a treated patient. The serial imaging and invasive sampling reflected case-specific decisions and should not be interpreted as a routine protocol for pneumonia.

title_zh: 混合性肺炎合并肺栓塞和支气管肺泡灌洗液中检测到的多种病原体:A 病例报告。
source_body_en: Severe community-acquired pneumonia may involve mixed pathogens and concurrent vascular complications. A 72-year-old man presented with fever, nonproductive cough, vomiting, hypoxemia, markedly elevated inflammatory markers, and an elevated D-dimer concentration. Chest computed tomography showed left lower-lobe consolidation and pleural effusion. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography, obtained because of hypoxemia and suspected pulmonary embolism, showed a filling defect in a right upper-lobe pulmonary artery. The patient received antimicrobial therapy prior to bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL). Bronchoscopy was performed in the bronchopulmonary segment corresponding to the radiographic lesion, and approximately 10 mL of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) was recovered aseptically for microbiological and cytological testing. An aliquot of at least 3 mL was allocated to a multiplex pathogen-targeted sequencing assay, which detected Chlamydia psittaci, influenza A H3N2, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and additional conditionally pathogenic or commensal organisms. The three principal detections were interpreted in conjunction with the clinical presentation, imaging, inflammatory markers, BALF cytology, conventional testing, and treatment response. The patient improved during antimicrobial and anticoagulant treatment and was discharged on December 3, 2025. At the documented outpatient follow-up on December 17, rivaroxaban was continued for approximately one further month. This case highlights the adjunctive value and interpretive limitations of targeted sequencing in a treated patient. The serial imaging and invasive sampling reflected case-specific decisions and should not be interpreted as a routine protocol for pneumonia.
abstract_zh: 严重的社区获得性肺炎可能涉及混合病原体并并发血管并发症。一名 72 岁男性出现发烧、干咳、呕吐、低氧血症、炎症标志物显着升高以及 D-二聚体浓度升高。胸部计算机断层扫描显示左下叶实变和胸腔积液。由于低氧血症和疑似肺栓塞而进行的计算机断层扫描肺血管造影显示右上叶肺动脉充盈缺损。患者在支气管肺泡灌洗(BAL)之前接受了抗菌治疗。在与放射学病变相对应的支气管肺段进行支气管镜检查,并无菌回收约10 mL的支气管肺泡灌洗液(BALF)用于微生物学和细胞学检测。将至少 3 mL 的等分试样分配给多重病原体靶向测序测定,该测定检测鹦鹉热衣原体、甲型 H3N2 流感、肺炎链球菌和其他条件致病性或共生生物。结合临床表现、影像学、炎症标志物、BALF 细胞学、常规测试和 治疗 反应来解释这三个主要检测结果。该患者在使用抗菌剂和抗凝剂 治疗 期间病情有所改善,并于 2025 年 12 月 3 日出院。在 12 月 17 日记录的门诊随访中,利伐沙班又持续了大约一个月。该案例凸显了靶向测序在治疗患者中的辅助价值和解释局限性。连续成像和侵入性采样反映了针对具体病例的决定,不应被解释为肺炎的常规方案。

title: Matrix Metalloproteinase-8 Deficiency Alters the Balance Between Viral Clearance and Immunopathology in H1N1 Infection.
abstract: Matrix metalloproteinase-8 (MMP-8) regulates inflammatory responses, but its contributions to the pathogenesis of influenza A viral (IAV) disease are not known. Plasma MMP-8 levels were increased 30-fold in subjects infected with H1N1 or seasonal IAV and were inversely associated with the PaO2/FiO2 ratio, suggesting potential value as a candidate marker of lung injury severity that requires validation in larger cohorts. MMP-8 levels were elevated in the lungs of H1N1-infected wild-type (WT) mice and localized to airway epithelial cells, macrophages, and polymorphonuclear neutrophils (PMNs). H1N1-infected Mmp-8-/- mice exhibited lower mortality and reduced lung viral burdens, but developed more severe lung injury than WT mice. Gene expression profiling revealed enhanced necroptosis and an exaggerated immune response in the lungs of infected Mmp-8-/- mice. Infected Mmp-8-/- mice had increased airway epithelial necroptosis with higher pulmonary levels of Type I interferons (IFNs), and increased frequencies of Class II MHC molecule-expressing macrophages and CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, and higher levels of some Th1 cytokines. In vitro, MMP-8 cleaved IL-1β and IL-6, but not Type I IFNs. These findings suggest that Mmp-8 deficiency is associated with restricted influenza virus spread and increased lung injury, accompanied by enhanced Type I IFN-associated necroptotic signaling and augmented antiviral immune responses. The latter may partly involve loss of MMP-8-mediated processing of pro-inflammatory mediators. MMP-8 may represent a host-response target in severe influenza infection, although therapeutic strategies targeting MMP-8 will need to balance enhanced viral clearance against the risk of increased lung immunopathology.

title_zh: 基质金属蛋白酶-8缺乏改变H1N1感染中病毒清除与免疫病理之间的平衡。
source_body_en: Matrix metalloproteinase-8 (MMP-8) regulates inflammatory responses, but its contributions to the pathogenesis of influenza A viral (IAV) disease are not known. Plasma MMP-8 levels were increased 30-fold in subjects infected with H1N1 or seasonal IAV and were inversely associated with the PaO2/FiO2 ratio, suggesting potential value as a candidate marker of lung injury severity that requires validation in larger cohorts. MMP-8 levels were elevated in the lungs of H1N1-infected wild-type (WT) mice and localized to airway epithelial cells, macrophages, and polymorphonuclear neutrophils (PMNs). H1N1-infected Mmp-8-/- mice exhibited lower mortality and reduced lung viral burdens, but developed more severe lung injury than WT mice. Gene expression profiling revealed enhanced necroptosis and an exaggerated immune response in the lungs of infected Mmp-8-/- mice. Infected Mmp-8-/- mice had increased airway epithelial necroptosis with higher pulmonary levels of Type I interferons (IFNs), and increased frequencies of Class II MHC molecule-expressing macrophages and CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, and higher levels of some Th1 cytokines. In vitro, MMP-8 cleaved IL-1β and IL-6, but not Type I IFNs. These findings suggest that Mmp-8 deficiency is associated with restricted influenza virus spread and increased lung injury, accompanied by enhanced Type I IFN-associated necroptotic signaling and augmented antiviral immune responses. The latter may partly involve loss of MMP-8-mediated processing of pro-inflammatory mediators. MMP-8 may represent a host-response target in severe influenza infection, although therapeutic strategies targeting MMP-8 will need to balance enhanced viral clearance against the risk of increased lung immunopathology.

title: Protective Effects of Influenza B Neuraminidase Antibodies Against Symptomatic Influenza Virus Infection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Influenza vaccines are designed to induce hemagglutinin-inhibiting (HAI) antibodies rather than neuraminidase-inhibiting (NAI) antibodies; therefore, NAI antibodies' protective effects need further investigation. Neuraminidase-inhibiting antibodies' protective effects, independent of HAI antibodies, have been demonstrated for influenza A viruses, but not influenza B viruses (IBVs). METHODS: Employing H6NB reassortant virus targets, we evaluated NAI antibodies' protective effects against IBV in sera from a prospective influenza vaccine effectiveness study among healthcare personnel (HCP) in Israel. Antibody titers against B/Brisbane/60/2008 and B/Phuket/3073/2013 were quantified by HAI and NAI assays. Matched NAI and HAI antibody titers from baseline and postvaccination sera were analyzed for the 2017-2018 influenza season. RESULTS: Laboratory-confirmed IBV infection was recorded in 64/262 HCP and influenza vaccination in 187/262 HCP. Vaccination did not consistently elicit rising NAI titers against vaccine strain B/Brisbane, with a geometric mean fold rise of 1.1 (95% CI: .9-1.3). However, comparing baseline NAI titers, geometric mean titer ratios were 1.50 (95% CI: 1.0-2.1) times higher against B/Brisbane and 2.5 (95% CI: 1.7-3.6) times higher against circulating B/Phuket in vaccinated versus unvaccinated HCP. Each 2-fold rise in NAI antibody titers reduced the hazard of symptomatic infection by 42% (95% CI: 36%-48%) against B/Phuket and 23% (95% CI: 13%-33%) against B/Brisbane, adjusting for HAI titers. CONCLUSIONS: Neuraminidase-inhibiting antibodies were a strong correlate of protection against symptomatic IBV infection, with protective effects independent of those from HAI antibodies. These findings suggest that the use and standardization of neuraminidase content in influenza vaccines could provide broader protection against influenza.

CONCLUSIONS: Neuraminidase-inhibiting antibodies were a strong correlate of protection against symptomatic IBV infection, with protective effects independent of those from HAI antibodies. These findings suggest that the use and standardization of neuraminidase content in influenza vaccines could provide broader protection against influenza.

title_zh: 乙型流感神经氨酸酶抗体对症状性流感病毒感染的保护作用。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Influenza vaccines are designed to induce hemagglutinin-inhibiting (HAI) antibodies rather than neuraminidase-inhibiting (NAI) antibodies; therefore, NAI antibodies' protective effects need further investigation. Neuraminidase-inhibiting antibodies' protective effects, independent of HAI antibodies, have been demonstrated for influenza A viruses, but not influenza B viruses (IBVs). METHODS: Employing H6NB reassortant virus targets, we evaluated NAI antibodies' protective effects against IBV in sera from a prospective influenza vaccine effectiveness study among healthcare personnel (HCP) in Israel. Matched NAI and HAI antibody titers from baseline and postvaccination sera were analyzed for the 2017-2018 influenza season. RESULTS: Laboratory-confirmed IBV infection was recorded in 64/262 HCP and influenza vaccination in 187/262 HCP. Vaccination did not consistently elicit rising NAI titers against vaccine strain B/Brisbane, with a geometric mean fold rise of 1.1 (95% CI: .9-1.3). Each 2-fold rise in NAI antibody titers reduced the hazard of symptomatic infection by 42% (95% CI: 36%-48%) against B/Phuket and 23% (95% CI: 13%-33%) against B/Brisbane, adjusting for HAI titers. CONCLUSIONS: Neuraminidase-inhibiting antibodies were a strong correlate of protection against symptomatic IBV infection, with protective effects independent of those from HAI antibodies. These findings suggest that the use and standardization of neuraminidase content in influenza vaccines could provide broader protection against influenza.
abstract_zh: 背景:流感疫苗疫苗旨在诱导血凝素抑制(HAI)抗体,而非神经氨酸酶抑制(NAI)抗体;因此,需要进一步研究NAI抗体的保护作用。对于流感A病毒,神经氨酸酶抑制抗体的保护作用已被证明,但尚未在流感B病毒(IBVs)中得到证实。方法:我们采用H6NB重配病毒作为靶标,在以色列的医疗工作者(HCP)中进行前瞻性流感疫苗接种有效性研究,评估NAI抗体对IBV的保护作用。通过HAI和NAI试验定量测定针对B/Brisbane/60/2008和B/Phuket/3073/2013的抗体滴度。分析了2017-2018流感季节基线和疫苗接种后血清中匹配的NAI和HAI抗体滴度。结果:实验室确认的IBV感染在64/262名HCP中被记录,而流感疫苗接种感染在187/262名HCP中被记录。疫苗接种并未一致诱导针对疫苗株B/Brisbane的NAI滴度上升,几何均数滴度上升为1.1(95% CI:.9-1.3)。然而,与未接种疫苗的HCP相比,接种疫苗的HCP针对B/Brisbane的基线NAI滴度几何均数滴度比为1.50(95% CI:1.0-2.1),针对流行B/Phuket的几何均数滴度比为2.5(95% CI:1.7-3.6)。在调整HAI滴度后,针对B/Phuket的NAI抗体滴度每上升2倍,症状性感染的危险性降低42%(95% CI:36%-48%),针对B/Brisbane的危险性降低23%(95% CI:13%-33%)。结论:神经氨酸酶抑制抗体是针对症状性IBV感染的强保护相关因素,其保护作用独立于血凝素抑制抗体的作用。这些发现表明,在流感疫苗中使用和标准化神经氨酸酶成分可能提供更广泛的流感保护。

title: Immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine in adults living with HIV compared with HIV-uninfected adults: a study from China
abstract: Objective To evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV3) in adults aged ≥18 years living with HIV and to provide evidence supporting influenza vaccination in this population in China. Methods This single-center, open-label comparative analysis was derived from a larger three-arm clinical study. For the present comparative analysis, 472 vaccinated participants were planned, including 236 adults living with HIV (Group 1) and 236 age- and sex-comparable HIV-uninfected adults (Group 2). Participants in both groups received one dose of IIV3 (0.5 mL) on Day 0. Blood samples were collected before and 28 days after vaccination for hemagglutination inhibition (HI) antibody testing against A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria strains. Immunogenicity endpoints included seroconversion rate, seroprotection rate, geometric mean titer (GMT), and geometric mean increase (GMI). Safety was assessed by monitoring solicited and unsolicited adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) during 6 months of follow-up. An unvaccinated cohort of adults living with HIV from the original trial was included only for an exploratory, descriptive analysis of influenza-like illness (ILI), without assessment of vaccine efficacy. Results A total of 489 participants were enrolled, including 237 in Group 1 and 252 in Group 2. At 28 days post-vaccination, seroconversion rates did not differ significantly between Group 1 and Group 2 for A(H1N1) (91.00% vs. 86.69%, P > 0.05), but significantly lower for A(H3N2) (49.50% vs. 89.52%) and B/Victoria (40.00% vs. 64.52%) (both P < 0.001). Seroprotection rates were also lower in Group 1 than in Group 2 for A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria (94.00% vs. 97.18%, and 40.50% vs. 68.55%, respectively). Post-vaccination GMTs were significantly lower in Group 1 for all three strains (all P < 0.001). GMI was higher for A(H1N1) but lower for A(H3N2) and B/Victoria in Group 1 than in Group 2 (all P < 0.001). Multivariable analyses showed that HIV infection remained independently associated with several measures of vaccine-induced immune responses after adjustment for demographic and clinical factors, particularly for A(H3N2). IIV3 was generally safe and well tolerated. Most AEs were mild in severity, and no Grade 4 adverse reactions or vaccine-related SAEs were reported. During the period from 29 days to 6 months after vaccination, few influenza-like illness events were reported among vaccinated and unvaccinated participants living with HIV; these findings were descriptive and were not used to assess vaccine efficacy against influenza. Conclusion Adults living with HIV developed substantial antibody responses following IIV3 vaccination, although the magnitude of response varied across influenza strains. A(H1N1) seroconversion was high in adults living with HIV, whereas responses to A(H3N2) and B/Victoria were generally lower than those in HIV-uninfected adults. HIV infection remained associated with reduced vaccine-induced immune responses for several strain-specific outcomes after multivariable adjustment, with associations particularly evident for A(H3N2). IIV3 was safe and well tolerated, supporting current recommendations for influenza vaccination in adults living with HIV. Clinical trial registration https://www.chictr.org.cn/showprojEN.html?proj=255613 , identifier ChiCTR2500112191.

source_records.title: Immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine in adults living with HIV compared with HIV-uninfected adults: a study from China
source_records.abstract: Objective To evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV3) in adults aged ≥18 years living with HIV and to provide evidence supporting influenza vaccination in this population in China. Methods This single-center, open-label comparative analysis was derived from a larger three-arm clinical study. For the present comparative analysis, 472 vaccinated participants were planned, including 236 adults living with HIV (Group 1) and 236 age- and sex-comparable HIV-uninfected adults (Group 2). Participants in both groups received one dose of IIV3 (0.5 mL) on Day 0. Blood samples were collected before and 28 days after vaccination for hemagglutination inhibition (HI) antibody testing against A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria strains. Immunogenicity endpoints included seroconversion rate, seroprotection rate, geometric mean titer (GMT), and geometric mean increase (GMI). Safety was assessed by monitoring solicited and unsolicited adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) during 6 months of follow-up. An unvaccinated cohort of adults living with HIV from the original trial was included only for an exploratory, descriptive analysis of influenza-like illness (ILI), without assessment of vaccine efficacy. Results A total of 489 participants were enrolled, including 237 in Group 1 and 252 in Group 2. At 28 days post-vaccination, seroconversion rates did not differ significantly between Group 1 and Group 2 for A(H1N1) (91.00% vs. 86.69%, P > 0.05), but significantly lower for A(H3N2) (49.50% vs. 89.52%) and B/Victoria (40.00% vs. 64.52%) (both P < 0.001). Seroprotection rates were also lower in Group 1 than in Group 2 for A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria (94.00% vs. 97.18%, and 40.50% vs. 68.55%, respectively). Post-vaccination GMTs were significantly lower in Group 1 for all three strains (all P < 0.001). GMI was higher for A(H1N1) but lower for A(H3N2) and B/Victoria in Group 1 than in Group 2 (all P < 0.001). Multivariable analyses showed that HIV infection remained independently associated with several measures of vaccine-induced immune responses after adjustment for demographic and clinical factors, particularly for A(H3N2). IIV3 was generally safe and well tolerated. Most AEs were mild in severity, and no Grade 4 adverse reactions or vaccine-related SAEs were reported. During the period from 29 days to 6 months after vaccination, few influenza-like illness events were reported among vaccinated and unvaccinated participants living with HIV; these findings were descriptive and were not used to assess vaccine efficacy against influenza. A(H1N1) seroconversion was high in adults living with HIV, whereas responses to A(H3N2) and B/Victoria were generally lower than those in HIV-uninfected adults. HIV infection remained associated with reduced vaccine-induced immune responses for several strain-specific outcomes after multivariable adjustment, with associations particularly evident for A(H3N2). IIV3 was safe and well tolerated, supporting current recommendations for influenza vaccination in adults living with HIV. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估三价灭活流感 疫苗 (IIV3) 在成人 HIV 感染者中的免疫原性和安全性,并为中国该人群中流感 疫苗 的支持提供证据。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项单中心、开放标签的比较分析源自一项更大规模的三组临床研究。它包括 472 名接种疫苗的参与者,其中 236 名感染艾滋病毒的成年人(第 1 组)和 236 名年龄和性别相当的未感染艾滋病毒的成年人(第 2 组)。
elements_zh.methods: 在 疫苗接种 之前和之后 28 天收集血样,用于针对 A(H1N1)、甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B/Victoria 毒株的血凝抑制 (HI) 抗体测试。通过在 6 个月的随访期间监测主动和主动不良事件 (AE) 以及严重不良事件 (SAE) 来评估安全性。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在多变量调整后,HIV 感染与 疫苗 诱导的 免疫应答 减少独立相关,对于几种毒株特异性结果,甲型H3N2流感病毒 的关联尤其明显。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持目前针对成人 HIV 感染者的流感 疫苗接种 的建议,因为 IIV3 通常是安全的且耐受性良好。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是单中心分析,结果可能无法推广到其他人群。由于该研究的观察性质以及缺乏对所有潜在混杂因素的控制,证据是中等的。

abstract_zh: 目的 评价三价灭活流感 疫苗 (IIV3) 在中国 18 岁以上成人 HIV 感染者中的免疫原性和安全性,为中国该人群感染 疫苗 流感提供证据。方法 这项单中心、开放标签的比较分析源自一项更大规模的三组临床研究。在本次比较分析中,计划有 472 名接种疫苗的参与者,其中包括 236 名感染艾滋病毒的成年人(第 1 组)和 236 名年龄和性别相当的未感染艾滋病毒的成年人(第 2 组)。两组参与者均在第 0 天接受一剂 IIV3 (0.5 mL)。在 疫苗接种 之前和之后 28 天收集血样,用于针对 A(H1N1)、甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B/Victoria 毒株的血凝抑制 (HI) 抗体测试。免疫原性终点包括血清转化率、血清保护率、几何平均滴度(GMT)和几何平均增加(GMI)。通过在 6 个月的随访期间监测主动和主动不良事件 (AE) 以及严重不良事件 (SAE) 来评估安全性。原始试验中未接种疫苗的 队列研究 成人 HIV 感染者仅用于对流感样疾病 (ILI) 进行探索性、描述性分析,未评估 疫苗 的疗效。结果 共有 489 名参与者入组,其中第 1 组 237 名,第 2 组 252 名。疫苗接种 后 28 天,A(H1N1) 组 1 和组 2 之间的血清转换率没有显着差异(91.00% vs. 86.69%,P > 0.05),但 甲型H3N2流感病毒 的血清转换率显着较低(49.50% 对比 89.52%)和 B/维多利亚(40.00% 对比 64.52%)(均 P < 0.001)。A(H1N1)、甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B/Victoria 的血清保护率在第 1 组中也低于第 2 组(分别为 94.00% vs. 97.18% 和 40.50% vs. 68.55%)。第 1 组中所有三种菌株的 疫苗接种 后 GMT 均显着较低(所有 P < 0.001)。第 1 组中 A(H1N1) 的 GMI 较高,但 甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B/Victoria 的 GMI 低于第 2 组(所有 P < 0.001)。多变量分析表明,在调整人口和临床因素(特别是 甲型H3N2流感病毒)后,HIV 感染仍然与 疫苗 诱导的 免疫应答 的多项测量值独立相关。IIV3 通常是安全且耐受性良好的。大多数 AE 的严重程度较轻,没有报告 4 级不良反应或 疫苗 相关的 SAE。在 疫苗接种 后 29 天至 6 个月期间,接种疫苗和未接种疫苗的 HIV 感染者中几乎没有报告流感样疾病事件;这些发现是描述性的,并不用于评估 疫苗 对流感的功效。结论 成人 HIV 感染者在 IIV3 疫苗接种 后产生了显着的抗体反应,尽管反应的程度因流感毒株而异。在感染 HIV 的成年人中,A(H1N1) 血清转化率较高,而对 甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B/Victoria 的反应通常低于未感染 HIV 的成年人。在多变量调整后,HIV 感染仍然与 疫苗 诱导的 免疫应答 减少有关,对于几种毒株特异性结果,甲型H3N2流感病毒 的关联尤其明显。IIV3 安全且耐受性良好,支持当前针对成人 HIV 感染者流感 疫苗接种 的建议。临床试验注册https://www.chictr.org.cn/showprojEN.html?proj=255613,标识符ChiCTR2500112191。

title: Polyclonal breast milk–derived secretory IgA confers broad antiviral protection against multiple respiratory viruses
abstract: Passive immunization is an important tool for protecting individuals with primary immune deficiencies from infectious diseases and offers a rapid response strategy for protecting vulnerable populations, particularly during the interval between pathogen emergence and vaccine deployment. Current approaches rely on intravenous delivery of IgG-enriched plasma or monoclonal antibodies, which limits accessibility, scalability, and effectiveness at mucosal surfaces, the primary entry point for respiratory viruses. Here, we tested LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from pooled human breast milk, to address these limitations. LCTG-001 demonstrated broad antiviral activity against clinically relevant respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus. LCTG-001 effectively recognized both group 1 and group 2 influenza A subtypes, including the highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, and engaged nonneutralizing effector mechanisms such as neuraminidase inhibition and neutrophil activation. When administered intranasally, LCTG-001 conferred complete protection against influenza A challenge in both immunocompetent and antibody-deficient murine models, preventing morbidity and mortality through a transient early reduction in viral burden followed by sustained improvements in lung pathology and lung barrier integrity. These findings highlight the potential of breast milk-derived secretory IgA as a scalable, mucosa-targeted passive immunization strategy capable of addressing both endemic and emerging respiratory viral threats.
